title: Casper and the Veil
premise: Noor Yarrow, a royal food-taster whose body has learned to survive poison, secretly keeps the ledgers of the Veil Guild, which trades in impossible things: borrowed years, returned voices, memories sold by weight. When the crown declares a hunt for anyone carrying 'the gift,' Noor is exposed and conscripted to reforge the broken covenant between the human realm and the Veil, a pact his own guild helped shatter. Guided by Casper, a memory-keeper who has forgotten everything except Noor's name, he must choose between loyalty to the guild that raised him and the truth that will save both realms. In the end Noor pays the covenant's price with his own immunity — surrendering every poison he has ever survived — and Casper trades her stolen memories to seal the new Veil, leaving them strangers who choose to begin again.
about_author: Ulyana Iversen is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing trade ledgers from vanished merchant houses before turning to fiction. She writes fantasy about people whose quiet professions hide enormous power, and she lives near a harbor where fog still arrives on schedule.

chapters.title: The Taster's Tongue
chapters.summary: POV Noor. At a royal banquet, Noor detects hemlock in the chancellor's wine and saves a life no one thanks him for. Afterward he slips into the Veil Guild's back office to balance its impossible ledgers. The beat: competence masking loneliness; we see how thoroughly he lives two lives.

chapters.title: Goods That Should Not Exist
chapters.summary: POV Noor. Auditing the guild's inventory, Noor finds a vial of someone's first love and a jar of unspent grief, and meets Casper, the memory-keeper who catalogs them but cannot remember her own past. The beat: wonder laced with unease as the trade's true cost surfaces.

chapters.title: The Proclamation
chapters.summary: POV Noor. Criers announce the crown's hunt for the gifted: registration, branding, conscription. Guildmaster Oren Vey burns three ledgers and orders silence. Noor realizes his taster's immunity marks him as clearly as any spell. The beat: dread arriving in daylight, ordinary streets turned hostile.

chapters.title: What Casper Keeps
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Casper tends the memory-vaults and reveals she traded her own past to save the guild years ago — all of it except one stubborn fragment: Noor's name. She warns him the vaults are failing since the covenant broke. The beat: tenderness shadowed by sacrifice already made.

chapters.title: A Knock at the Ledgers
chapters.summary: POV Noor. A royal inquisitor, Dame Serah Kolt, traces a purchased memory to the guild and interrogates Noor under cover of a routine tasting audit. He lies well, but she leaves a mark on his door. The beat: the hunter's patience; fear sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Oren's Bargain
chapters.summary: POV Noor. Guildmaster Vey confesses the guild brokered the covenant's breaking, selling the Veil's anchor-stone to the crown for protection. He asks Noor to steal it back. The beat: betrayal reframed as desperation; loyalty beginning to crack.

chapters.title: Into the Undercellar
chapters.summary: POV Noor. Noor and Casper descend through the guild's oldest cellar into the thin place where the Veil once stood — now a wound of gray static. They find the anchor-stone's empty cradle and a message scratched in old script: the price returns. The beat: awe curdling into responsibility.

chapters.title: The Hunt Begins
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Crown riders seize gifted citizens in the market square; a child who mends broken cups is taken screaming. Casper uses a stored memory to mask Noor's signature, spending something irreplaceable. The beat: guilt and urgency braided together.

chapters.title: Dame Serah's Offer
chapters.summary: POV Noor. Serah corners Noor privately: she knows what he is. She offers immunity for the whole guild if he helps the crown control the anchor-stone instead of restoring it. The beat: temptation with a reasonable face; duty pulling against truth.

chapters.title: Ledgers of the Broken Year
chapters.summary: POV Noor. Decoding Vey's hidden books, Noor learns the covenant failed because the Veil's side was cheated — the guild sold their anchor and blamed them for the breach. The beat: cold clarity; the enemy was always inside the walls.

chapters.title: Casper's Fragment
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Chasing her one surviving memory, Casper relives the night she gave up her past: she was the Veil's own envoy, and she chose exile to warn the humans. Her love for Noor predates her forgetting. The beat: heartbreak and revelation entwined.

chapters.title: The Vault Burns
chapters.summary: POV Noor. Serah raids the guildhall; Vey dies defending the ledgers, and the memory-vault ignites, releasing decades of traded lives into the street like migrating birds. Noor saves one crate: the covenant's original terms. The beat: catastrophic loss becoming a single thread of hope.

chapters.title: Fugitives on the Salt Road
chapters.summary: POV Noor. Noor and Casper flee the city with the terms hidden in a spice shipment, pursued by Serah and haunted by freed memories that recognize Casper and call her by an older name. The beat: road-worn intimacy deepening under pressure.

chapters.title: The Inn of Borrowed Years
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Sheltering at a guild safehouse run by an aged broker, they learn the covenant can be reforged only at the Veil's threshold during the dark of the moon — six days away — and only if a mortal pays in kind. The beat: brief warmth before the bill comes due.

chapters.title: Serah's Truth
chapters.summary: POV Noor. Serah catches them, but Noor shows her the ledgers proving the crown's own ministers caused the breach. Shaken, she gives them a day's head start — and keeps hunting, because duty is all she has. The beat: antagonist humanized; the theme of loyalty vs. truth made flesh.

chapters.title: The Gray Wound
chapters.summary: POV Noor. They reach the thin place as reality frays around it; the Veil's exiled envoy — Casper's own kin — bars the way, demanding proof that humans deserve a second covenant. The beat: judgment day atmosphere; Noor offering honesty over persuasion.

chapters.title: Price of Immunity
chapters.summary: POV Noor. The terms demand payment in kind: the Veil gave its memory; mortals must give their armor. Noor understands — his hard-won immunity to every poison must be surrendered. He signs without hesitation. The beat: quiet, terrifying resolve; love against duty resolved in action.

chapters.title: Dark of the Moon
chapters.summary: POV Casper. At the threshold, Casper completes the rite by returning her final fragment — the memory of choosing Noor — as the anchor-stone's replacement. The Veil seals; both realms breathe again. The beat: climax rendered as sacrifice rather than battle.

chapters.title: What the Poison Remembers
chapters.summary: POV Noor. Powerless and mortal for the first time, Noor faces Serah one last time and survives not by immunity but because she chooses, finally, to tell the truth to the crown. The beat: vulnerability as strength; the hunt ends with testimony, not blood.

chapters.title: Strangers at the Door
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Memoryless and mortal, Casper opens the rebuilt guildhall's door to a man she doesn't know who somehow knows her tea order exactly. The beat: bittersweet comedy; grief and possibility sharing a table.

chapters.title: New Ledgers
chapters.summary: POV Noor. Noor reopens the guild under a new charter — trade in impossible things, but fair this time, with the Veil as partner. He begins teaching Casper who she was, one true story a night. The beat: rebuilding as devotion; hope earned, not given.

chapters.title: The First Dish
chapters.summary: POV Noor. Months later, Noor cooks a meal containing no poison for the first time in his adult life, and Casper remembers something new on her own: his laugh. The covenant holds; so do they. The beat: resolution as a small, chosen future — memory and love beginning again from zero.
